chunks: And from him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"The child, when he is capable of fasting three consecutive days, then fasting of the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him."
ai.seo_question: When does fasting become obligatory for a child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* defines the threshold of *bulugh* (maturity) for fasting not by age, but by physical capacity (*itaqa*), specifically the ability to fast three consecutive days without undue hardship. This criterion serves as a practical preparatory test, ensuring the child can sustain the full month’s obligation, thereby distinguishing between mere capability and the actual imposition of duty (*wujub*).
